messages.subject: Help with computational issues R-INLA
parts:
Hello everyone. I'm working on a master thesis project, and my goal is to compute predictions for NO₂ concentrations in the Po Valley. I have a dataset with daily records measured by 168 stations located in the designated area (dati_completi_df). 

My data contain the following information:

  • mean_NO₂: the response variable
  • Altitude, Longitude, Latitude
  • mean_NO₂_c: NO₂ concentrations measured by Copernicus.
  • Date: a variable indicating the day of measurement
  • AirQualityStationEoICode: an identifier for each station
I also built a prediction grid (grigliato_previsione) with the same information, except for the AirQualityStationEoICode, which I would like to use to build prediction maps. 

Here is my code, which is based on Blangiardo, Micheletti (2015) example for PM10 predictions in Piemonte:

train_sf <- dati_completi_df |>
  dplyr::filter(Date < "2023-12-01")  # train set from 2023-01-01 to 2023-11-30

test_sf <- dati_completi_df |>
  dplyr::filter(Date >= "2023-12-01") # test set from 2023-12-01 to 2023-12-31

n_station <- length(unique(train_sf$AirQualityStationEoICode))
n_data <- nrow(train_sf)
n_days <- n_data/n_station

train_sf$time <- rep(1:n_days, times = n_station)

coordinates.allyear <- as.matrix(train_sf[, c("Longitude", "Latitude")] |>
                                   st_drop_geometry())  

limiti <- st_coordinates(contorno)[, c("X", "Y")]  #contorno is an sf object containing the area of interest

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = coordinates.allyear,
                     loc.domain = limiti,
                     offset = c(0.3, 0.5),
                     max.edge = c(0.5, 1))

mesh$n #699

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh, alpha = 2)

A_est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh,
                          loc = coordinates.allyear,
                          group = train_sf$time,
                          n.group = n_days)

dim(A_est)   # 56112  233466

s_index <- inla.spde.make.index(name="spatial.field",
                                n.spde = spde$n.spde,
                                n.group = n_days)


stack_est <- inla.stack(data = list(mean_NO2 = train_sf$mean_NO2),
                        A = list(A_est, 1),
                        effects = list(c(s_index,list(Intercept = 1)),
                                     list(data.frame(Altitude = train_sf$Altitude,
                                            mean_NO2_c = train_sf$mean_NO2_c))),
                        tag = "est")


grigliato_previsione$time <- rep(1:length(unique(grigliato_previsione$Date)),
                                 times = length(unique(grigliato_previsione$ID)))


gg <- grigliato_previsione |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% 335:365)

gg <- gg[1, ] # prediction only on one point and one time stamp

A_pred <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh,
                           loc = cbind(gg$Longitude, gg$Latitude),
                           group = gg$time,
                           n.group = n_days + length(unique(gg$time)))

dim(A_pred) # 1  234165

s_index_pred <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial.field",
                                     n.spde = spde$n.spde,
                                     n.group = n_days + length(unique(gg$time)))

stack_pred <- inla.stack(data = list(mean_NO2 = NA),
                         A = list(A_pred, 1),
                         effects = list(c(s_index_pred, list(Intercept = 1)),
                                      list(data.frame(Altitude = gg$Altitude,
                                                      mean_NO2_c = gg$mean_NO2_c))),
                         tag = "pred")

stack <- inla.stack(stack_est, stack_pred)

formula <- mean_NO2 ~ -1 + Intercept + f(spatial.field, model = spde,
                          group = spatial.field.group, control.group = list(model = "rw1")) +
  Altitude + mean_NO2_c


output <- inla(formula,
               data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde = spde),
               family ="gaussian", quantiles = NULL,
               control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack), compute = TRUE),
               control.compute = list(return.marginals.predictor = F),
               control.inla = list(strategy = "simplified.laplace", int.strategy = "ccd"),
               num.threads = 2)

output

My model takes AGES just to predict one point at one time stamp and I'm a little bit discouraged. Do you have any suggestion? Am I doing something wrong? I'm not so familiar with the R-INLA package. 

Thank you so much in advance, 
Alessia
